title: An SAE Feature Can Be Interpretable and Still Be Useless for Steering
hook: Sparse-autoencoder features with clean descriptions often steer badly or backwards. Studying what they do to the logits explains why: few features act as reusable directions.
key_points: The known problem: features with clear activation descriptions can have weak, unexpected, or opposite causal effects, and steering varies across prompts.
Prior work analyzed feature geometry inside the model; this paper analyzes the geometry of the logit changes an intervention causes.
FEGA is unsupervised: remove the same active SAE feature across many contexts and study the resulting cloud of logit changes.
Across SAE variants, consistent one-dimensional effects are rare — few features behave like reusable directions.
Value-like features (static information, e.g. factual attributes) more often show structured low-dimensional effects, though usually spanning several directions.
Pointer-like features (context-dependent operations) show predominantly diffuse effects — interpretable and causally relevant, but with no stable steering direction.
content_html: Sparse autoencoders are the workhorse of modern interpretability, and they carry a persistent embarrassment: a feature whose activations have a clean, human-readable description will often steer weakly, unpredictably, or in the wrong direction. Selecting features by activation can also miss the ones that would actually produce the output change you want.
extra_html:
Looking downstream instead of inside

Most geometric analysis of SAE features has studied where they sit in the model's representation space — where they're computed. Hoang and colleagues invert that. Their Feature-Effect Geometry Analysis (FEGA) is unsupervised: take one active SAE feature, remove it across many different contexts, and examine the resulting cloud of logit changes. If a feature were a reusable steering direction, that cloud would be essentially one-dimensional.

Across SAE variants, it usually isn't. Consistent one-dimensional effects are rare.

Two kinds of feature

To make sense of the variation, the authors distinguish value-like features, tied to static information such as factual attributes, from pointer-like features, associated with context-dependent operations. Value-like features more often show structured, low-dimensional effects — though typically still spanning several directions. Pointer-like features are predominantly diffuse. The conclusion is a useful caution rather than a dismissal: interpretability and causal relevance do not imply steerability, and a feature can have all three properties come apart.

related.title: SAE Interventions Are Unreliable
related.hook: Clamping a 'harmful' sparse-autoencoder feature looks like it stops bad behavior — but this paper recovers it 95.8% of the time, exposing the gap between feature-level and real control.

related.title: Scaling and Evaluating Sparse Autoencoders
related.hook: Tuning the sparsity penalty on an autoencoder is fiddly. Use a top-k constraint instead and you can dial sparsity directly — and scale SAEs to GPT-4.

flashcards.prompt: What does FEGA measure that prior SAE geometry work did not?
flashcards.back_html: The geometry of effects: it ablates the same active feature across many contexts and analyzes the resulting cloud of logit changes — downstream of the model, rather than the geometry of where features live inside it.

flashcards.prompt: What distinguishes 'value-like' from 'pointer-like' SAE features in this analysis?

choices.text: Value-like features encode static information and tend to have structured low-dimensional effects; pointer-like features encode context-dependent operations and have diffuse effects
Value-like features activate more frequently, pointer-like features more sparsely
Value-like features live in early layers, pointer-like features in late layers

flashcards.explanation_html: The split is functional: features tied to static facts produce comparatively structured effects (still usually spanning several directions), while features associated with context-dependent operations scatter their effects across many directions.

flashcards.prompt: What is the paper's headline caution for anyone steering models with SAE features?
flashcards.back_html: A feature can be genuinely interpretable and genuinely causally relevant without providing a stable direction to steer along — consistent one-dimensional effects turn out to be rare across SAE variants.
